The problem is that we don't know what your friend did. The fact that folders are missing confirms that the transfer was not done correctly. If the old PC you transferred from is still available follow these steps:

BACKUP

  1. ensure thunderbird is not running
  2. enter %appdata% in search window on task bar and press Enter key
  3. this should open windows file explorer in Appdata\roaming folder
  4. highlight the Thunderbird folder and copy to external media

RESTORE

  1. ensure thunderbird is installed, run once, and NOT running
  2. enter %appdata% in search window on task bar and press Enter key
  3. delete the thunderbird folder
  4. you should be in Appdata\roaming folder , copy&paste the exported Thunderbird folder there.
  5. start thunderbird and all should be there

content:
Hello there


You seem to have a bug in your Thunderbird email software. The first thing to do is run a full antivirus scan and try to quarantine the infected email. And try to find a way to clean it: start Thunderbird in Troubleshoot Mode, compact folders, and delete bad or damaged add-ons or extensions

If the Thunderbird software is infected or behaving strangely, you may need to reset or reinstall the entire program.

Because Thunderbird stores your emails in a local profile folder rather than within the application itself, the issue could stem from a corrupted email file, a bad extension, or infected files.

You can try to clean the software or > replace it >with a fresh installation of the thunderbird software.

Use https://download.mozilla.org/?product=thunderbird-150.0.2-SSL&os=win&lang=en-US

https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/new-thunderbird-desktop

https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/troubleshoot-mode-thunderbird


Tip An accidental bug can get into the profile map and cause problems.
